memory_candidates.content: A shell script deployed per-repo as `<repo>/.claude/scripts/<name>.sh` (or similar) that resolves its own project root via `PROJECT_ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")"/../.. && pwd)"` derives that root from the SCRIPT's own on-disk location, not from `$PWD`/the invoking shell's cwd. Invoking a copy of such a script from a different location (e.g. the source-store copy, by absolute path, after `cd`-ing into a target repo) does NOT make it operate against that target repo -- it silently resolves paths relative to wherever the invoked script file itself lives. This can produce a misleading empty/no-op result (e.g. 'sub-index missing, exit 0') that looks like a valid but uninteresting outcome rather than a broken test setup. When a plan instructs 'cd into repo X, then invoke script Y by absolute path' for a script with this resolution pattern, verify the resolution empirically first; if it doesn't reach the target code path, build an equivalent scratch harness that mirrors the real deploy directory shape (all sibling scripts + the target sub-index/data copied into a fake root at the same relative depth) rather than trusting the literal invocation.
